Measured 23138 at 2026-08-12 (v0.26.0: +733 total — +431 the four features, +302 the three-specialist adversarial round, whose recurring shape was PRODUCER-SIDE INVISIBILITY: all seven of the test-analyzer's mutations survived the original suite, because every canary proved the CONSUMING half (the mask in laneStates, the ledger gate, the deny path) while the producing half (noteLaneHealth, the limiter's Save-on-allow, the incident_mode_on wire, the config backfill) had zero coverage — the breaker's only writer could be deleted with green CI. The review round's lines: internal/orch/lockfile (~35, the ledger's O_CREATE|O_EXCL stale-steal lock extracted rather than copied a third time) + locked Update/Decide read-modify-write APIs on both state packages (parallel dispatches — strategy concurrency defaults to 2 — lost updates silently: a concurrent heal overwritten by a stale armed set, two dispatches both passing at limit−1; pid-unique tmp names + a brief rename retry for Windows' rename-under-reader Access-denied, empirically verified by review); a corrupt state file is now re-materialized clean by the next update instead of warning forever; the resil-alert latch + the status Resilience block (exclusions with exclusion.Reason — previously dead code — limiter stamps, state warnings, the persistence-failure latch), because the mechanisms' entire failure channel was stderr and the detached strategy runner wires stderr to the null device — a breaker that warns to nobody and keeps failing open protects nothing; incident mode's denominator narrowed to the CLASS'S CANDIDATE lanes (on a two-lane class, fleet pressure would have suspended the price past a calm candidate — the exact opposite of the rationale) and its engagement recorded on Decision.Incident + the reason string (a B8 feature whose engagement is invisible cannot accumulate promotion evidence); the exhausted+excluded resume merge takes the LATER instant and never downgrades a hard_stop/exhausted label to 'unavailable'; rate_limit_origin now stamps on ALL receipt paths (codex/glm classify only vendor output → upstream by construction); local limiter denials get the egress-style nothing-ran carve-out in the audit block (own counter, out of the coverage denominator); breaker fail-streaks decay after 6h quiet (one January spawn_error plus one in June is not consecutive); ExclusionOff is threaded from the caller's already-loaded cfg so a mid-dispatch config edit cannot split recorder from router. Declined with reason: exclusion backoff priors stay non-configurable this PR (the Options struct exists so a future orchcfg knob is a field addition; softened the comment that overclaimed) and empty_result does not arm the breaker (ambiguous between adapter garbage and honest model behavior; reopen if a real local-agent empty-loop shows up)) — feature accounting for the +431: internal/orch/exclusion (~170): the self-healing lane breaker — four features, each behind the smallest honest surface. internal/orch/exclusion (~170): the self-healing lane breaker — adapter failures (spawn_error/parse_error everywhere, api_error on local) arm a per-lane exclusion whose backoff doubles and caps; one success deletes the entry; expiry itself re-admits (a structural half-open probe, no probe scheduler to go wrong). Deliberately NOT wired to quota classes: rate_limit/refusal/exhausted are admission's and the lanes' — excluding on them would double-count pressure the router already prices. internal/orch/slidewin (~90): the local-lane sliding-window limiter — the local box serves the operator's interactive work too, and a fixed window allows a 2N burst straddling its reset instant, which is the failure the SLIDING window exists to close. router incident mode (~40): when a strict majority of lanes are pressured, the +1 shadow prices (throttle, downshift) are suspended — they exist to shed load onto calmer lanes, and with no calmer lanes they only shuffle work onto WORSE models; masking still applies (a dead lane never wins). Ships OFF behind incident_mode_on, the same B8 posture as pace_rank_on: routing-visible, promotes only through eval evidence — the canary proves the MECHANISM, not the policy. Typed 429 (~30 across claudelane/dispatch/run): RateLimitOrigin distinguishes the vendor's own 429 (upstream — ledger-eligible) from a limit OUR software imposed (local — must never mark the vendor window exhausted; a self-inflicted denial recorded as vendor truth poisons quota calibration from the inside). "" from pre-W6 producers stays upstream, fail-safe toward existing behavior. All state files fail OPEN with a warning when unreadable (absent-vs-undetermined: a breaker/limiter that cannot read its state must not invent exclusions or denials, and must say so). Wiring: laneStates masks excluded lanes as unavailable with the breaker's resume; noteLaneHealth feeds outcomes from all four lane runners; the limiter denial relegates (exit 3) with a typed receipt). Prior: 22405 at 2026-08-11 (v0.25.0: +509 total — +387 the dashboard, +122 the adversarial-review round, whose three MAJORs shared one shape: THE DASHBOARD'S CLEAN STATES WERE UNFALSIFIABLE. (1) `-json` on an absent log emitted prose with exit 0 — a machine consumer read a fresh install as 'nothing to report'; now a well-formed Report with log_absent:true. (2) A parseable receipt with a missing/zero ts unmarshals WITHOUT error (verified: `{}` and `null` decode into a zero Record), was silently window-filtered by -days — not in any table, and no WARN because the skipped counter never saw it — and under whole-log minted a year-1 span and a 0001-01-01 activity bucket; now a surfaced untimed_receipts counter, excluded from span/activity, excluded-but-announced under -days. (3) The silent-fallback detector's blindness rendered identically to health: nothing reported how many executed receipts carried NO attribution, so a regressed capture pipeline would read 'all clear' forever; now the fallback line always carries its own coverage — and the first live render proved the point: attribution present on 268/1031 executed on this machine's real log, i.e. the detector the operator would have trusted was blind on 74% of history. Minors folded in: write errors propagate (a truncated dashboard must not exit 0 when completeness is the acceptance contract), empty model/outcome bucket as '(none)' instead of vanishing from lines whose totals should reconcile, zero-denominator adherence renders n/a instead of a 0.0% that reads as maximal failure, attestation counters lost omitempty (0 is a claim, not an absence), from/to gained omitzero, -lane '(none)' selects empty-lane receipts and a lane miss prints the lanes actually present. Declined with reason: a >4MB line stays a loud torn-read error rather than a skipped line — the scanner cannot safely resynchronize past it, and a dashboard silently missing the log's tail is the exact lie this tool exists to end. The dashboard, one file (report.go). Its whole contract is honesty about the log it renders, and that is where the lines went: the activity window anchors to the newest RECEIPT's timestamp, never time.Now(), so a fixed log renders byte-identically forever (the acceptance gate's determinism clause — and the test fixture lives in 2020 precisely so a clock-anchored implementation fails loudly); corrupt JSONL lines are COUNTED and rendered as a WARN instead of silently skipped, because a dashboard that drops lines it cannot read while presenting itself as the whole log is the covered-everything lie; the read layer distinguishes absent (no log yet — a normal state) from unreadable/torn (the real error propagates, no partial dashboard), which is W7a's absent-vs-undetermined trichotomy applied at the file layer; and the requested→actual fallback-pair table exists because AttributedModels was designed as the silent-fallback detection signal (dispatch.go's own comment) and until now had no renderer anywhere. The lane table deliberately includes strategy steps in token/spend columns (burn is its point) while adherence percentages stay on audit.go's S2R-1/S3R-4 definitions via the embedded ReceiptsSummary — one taxonomy, two documented views, no second implementation of either). Prior: 21896 at 2026-08-11 (v0.24.0: +2354, the largest single increment in this project's history and the one that most needed the ratchet to force an argument for it. W7a is a feature that WRITES TO THE OPERATOR'S ~/.claude/settings.json, so the code that is not the feature is the code that keeps it from doing damage, and that is most of the line count. Roughly: ~600 for internal/orch/hostcfg (an order-preserving JSON editor; the obvious map[string]any implementation alphabetises every key and re-indents every nested value, which on a hand-maintained git-tracked settings.json is an unreadable whole-file diff on every install, so it was never a viable option), ~1050 for the install/uninstall state machine across three files (plan, read-only assess, apply with rollback, reverse), and the REMAINING ~700 is the adversarial-review round -- three fresh-context specialists, every finding reproduced against running code, every one ending in a damaged or unrecoverable operator config. Those seven: (1) any `claude` invocation, even a read-only `mcp list`, REWRITES settings.json (normalises `model`, re-indents), so hashing the bytes we wrote recorded a hash stale before install returned and the byte-identical restore path would have been dead code on every real machine -- hashes now come from disk after all steps; (2) a SECOND install overwrote the pre-install backup with already-installed bytes while the manifest kept install #1's hash, so the integrity check could never match again and uninstall hard-failed permanently with the config still wired; (3) an unparseable entry OF OURS read as 'already gone', so uninstall reported ok, deleted the manifest, and left the hook wired with nothing on disk claiming ownership -- absence must be PROVED, so the lookup gained a third answer, the same absent-vs-undetermined trichotomy Presence already carries for files; (4) a statusLine that was present but whose command could not be read (a `static` type, or the bare-string form) got the tee wired over it with an empty delegate, rendering a BLANK status bar from a run that reported success; (5) -home isolated only the host config, so a scratch install wrote its manifest, backups, tee and delegate into the operator's REAL ~/.meta-router, planting an ownership claim that then made the real install refuse permanently; (6) rollback ran forward, deleting the tee script before restoring the settings.json that referenced it, and reported failures only to stderr where they died with the scrollback; (7) the registry undo ran unprobed, so a server the operator had already removed made `claude mcp remove` exit 1 and abort the whole uninstall with everything still wired, on every retry. Also in that round: manifest steps are validated per kind before being acted on (an empty Ident made `strings.Contains(x, "")` true, so ANY operator statusLine read as ours and the restore wrote an absent Prior into the file), MemberSet/ArrayAppend refuse non-JSON (reindent fell back to its input on error, so an invalid value was stored, rendered and saved with a nil error -- the very corruption the package exists to prevent, arriving through the package itself), duplicate keys are refused rather than collapsed last-wins, CRLF/BOM/key-spelling/blank-line-indent are all preserved, and array entries are re-located by ident at removal time rather than by an index that goes stale after the first removal. The honest summary: the feature is ~1650 lines and the evidence that it is safe is ~700, and both numbers are the cost of a command whose failure mode is an operator's config). Prior: 19542 at 2026-08-11 (v0.23.0: +42, half of it the review round. Review caught that adding TYPED session_id/prompt_id fields made the payload type-checked where it was not before: a payload emitting either as a number decodes Prompt fine but returns UnmarshalTypeError, and the existing fatal-on-error branch would then surface NOTHING on every prompt while logging the misleading reason 'no prompt' -- a regression introduced by the very change adding the fields. Now gated on the prompt, not the error. Review also caught that the no-prompt-text test was TAUTOLOGICAL (it asserted a sample string was absent from a Record that never held it, so no change to Record could turn it red, including the one thing it claimed to prevent); replaced with an allowlist over Record's json tags that goes red on ANY new field. Original wiring was +21 to log session_id and prompt_id on every surfacing event. Claude Code supplies both on the UserPromptSubmit payload (prompt_id since v2.1.196; this fleet runs 2.1.219+), so an analytics join becomes an EXACT composite key instead of a timestamp window. The window join was session-BLIND and 72.4% of active 10-minute buckets have >1 session running, which inflated a recorded live metric from ~23% to a claimed 39.7%. Both fields are opaque identifiers, never prompt content, and both are omitempty so a build that does not supply them leaves the key ABSENT rather than writing an empty string a join would read as one shared session). Prior: 19500 at 2026-08-11 (v0.22.0: +102, which includes the adversarial-review round. Review reproduced that the FIRST draft of the ownership filter treated a NON-RESOLVING declaration as authority: a manifest saying './skills' (the dir itself) or a path to the SKILL.md yields a non-empty owned-set matching nothing, so the filter drops every skill and the pack harvests ZERO -- six live roots (40 skills) sit one upstream manifest edit from that, under the 30% removal guard. Authority must now RESOLVE to a real directory. It also decoded skills as []string, so ONE sibling plugin using the string form ('skills': './', as the live huggingface-skills manifest does) failed the whole document and silently switched ownership off for every pack in that marketplace. ParseSkillMD was deleted rather than left as a footgun -- it was dead after fix (a) and its only behaviour was the rule now established as wrong. Original wiring was +72 for two catalog-composition fixes, both measured on the live machine. (a) The skills walk required a `name:` frontmatter field and silently dropped anything without one -- while overwriting s.Name with the DIRECTORY name three lines later, so the requirement changed nothing except excluding valid skills; it dropped all 11 searchfit-seo skills, every one invocable. (b) A marketplace cache dir holds the WHOLE marketplace's skills while the installed plugin owns a subset, so harvesting it under one pack minted 13 uninvocable `document-skills:*` IDs which then won description-dedup and suppressed the real frontend-design:frontend-design and skill-creator:skill-creator. ownedSkillDirs reads the authoritative .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and filters ONLY when it names the pack, so every root without ownership data is untouched). Prior: 19398 at 2026-08-11 (v0.21.0: +287, of which ~150 are the adversarial-review round -- two reviewers independently reproduced that the FIRST draft (a) could not degrade at all for a SLOW reranker, because the fallback re-embedded and embed+rerank+embed cannot fit one deadline, so the likely failure mode produced 'deadline exceeded' and surfaced nothing; (b) recorded the degradation on only 1 of 5 outcome modes, leaving ~half of rows (gated-empty especially) byte-identical to healthy ones; (c) posted raw prompt text to an unprobed port, defeating the embed path's deliberate probe-before-send guard, and pinned the reranker to eps[0] while the embedder failed over; and (d) silently coerced a misspelled -ranker to embed. The fix restructures to embed-once-then-Reorder (degraded path is now free), adds a live-endpoint probe, a minimum-deadline guard, flag validation, and carries degradeErr out of the goroutine so every outcome records it. +137 was the original wiring to wire embed+rerank into PRODUCTION surfacing -- EmbedRerank.RetrieveScored (reranked ORDER, embed cosines preserved in .Score, primary topCos passed through so the -min-cosine gate admits exactly the same prompts as embed-only), the shared rerankOrder extracted so Retrieve and RetrieveScored can never disagree, and rerankOrEmbed in mr-hook. That last piece is the non-obvious cost: EmbedRerank propagates every failure BY DESIGN because a silent fallback would score embed-only under the embed+rerank label in the eval -- but in production that same strictness turns a reranker hiccup into decide() reporting embedder-down and surfacing NOTHING. rerankOrEmbed degrades to embed ORDER and rewrites the logged mode to "embed" so the row never claims a rerank that did not run).
